bull_bear.body: The stated framework is **organic plus inorganic**, with acquisition discipline articulated more clearly than usual: *"we as an organization have an organic plus inorganic growth ambition and thesis. So, we continue to be on the lookout… actively receiving inbounds."* The filter is explicit — *"we are also very, very careful in terms of only acquiring where the capability is differentiated, the offering will help us create basically a positive or accretive effect. And then the organization is able to offer both value as well as margin accretion"* — and the cadence is deliberately low: *"those things, they happen few and far in between."* The near-term priority is consolidation, not another deal: *"we right now are focused on making sure that we take full advantage of Novigo acquisition."* Everything else is P&L investment (AI, sales & marketing, go-to-market domain/technical hires). **No dividend, buyback, balance-sheet, net-debt or cash-balance figure was given on this call** — only the servicing cost (interest INR9.5 cr/quarter) and the FX book ($43.32 mn forward cover @ INR93.27).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **The margin guide is below the delivered margin.** 20.1% delivered against a reaffirmed sustainable **18–19%**. Management has pre-announced ~120bps of give-back; the question for next quarter is whether it arrives via FX reversal or reinvestment.
- **FX is doing a large, unquantified share of the work — and the hedges are now underwater.** Management concedes *"quite a large portion of it also comes from… rupee depreciation, which we cannot take for granted."* Meanwhile forward cover of **$43.32 mn sits at an average INR93.27 against a 30-Jun spot of INR94.66**, i.e. the hedged slice does not capture further depreciation; a **realised loss of INR9 cr** on forward settlements already hit this quarter's other income, and matured contracts are reclassifying accumulated OCI losses into the P&L. Other income has swung from **+INR13.1 cr to −INR0.87 cr in one quarter**.
- **TTM ACV bookings are flat ($82.9 mn vs $82.3 mn).** With H2 revenue explicitly framed as a function of H1 bookings, a flat booking series is the most direct constraint on the second-half acceleration management is hinting at.
- **Organic / constant-currency growth is the persistent bear point and was never quantified.** Asked directly — *"organic growth remains very muted… when we can expect some revival in that growth?"* — the answer was qualitative. The 3–4% CC ambition came with *"a small deviation obviously changes it to 2% or so"* and no timeline. Three analysts (Anmol Garg, Ashis Das, Sandeep Shah) circled the same gap.
- **Deal decision cycles.** *"the biggest factor over there continues to be the decision cycles, sometimes if a deal decision gets delayed."*
- **Discretionary, project-based revenue with low annuity.** *"being a project space business or discretionary spend business, we have to anticipate that the projects that we start will obviously come to an end. And hence, we have to continue to win more than what closes."* APAC already fell this quarter *"due to some of the larger projects… that came to an end."*
- **Novigo's Middle East exposure.** *"an ongoing geopolitical challenge that they are dealing with, which is due to the geopolitical situation in the Middle East."* MEA is only 3.6% of group revenue, which caps the direct damage.
- **Structurally elevated tax rate.** ETR ~31% vs normalized 28–29%, *"due to non-deductibility of amortization of intangible acquired through acquisition"* — persists while the intangibles run off.
- **Severance / redundancies.** Non-recurring costs are *"severance payment for certain redundant positions"*, unquantified — worth watching whether this recurs.
- **Rising client concentration.** Top client 5.8% → 6.0%, top 10 24.0% → 24.4%. Still low, but the direction is up and management frames it as a positive.
- **SG&A is a standing commitment, not a one-quarter step.** *"there is definitely a very deliberate focus and effort to increase sales and marketing in that area"* — operating leverage on this line should not be assumed.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
Confident but disciplined about what it will and will not say. The no-guidance policy was held under four separate attempts (full-year outlook, H2 ACV, quantifiable deal wins, CC-growth timing), and Nitesh Bansal declined gracefully rather than substituting vague numbers — *"I wish, that is a question I obviously keep asking myself, that is a million-dollar question."* The genuinely creditable moment was volunteering that FX, not execution, carries *"quite a large portion"* of the margin gain, and then reaffirming a **lower** 18–19% band rather than letting 20.1% stand as the new base — companies rarely talk their own quarter down. The AI-deflation answer was substantive rather than defensive, and correctly located the reason in contract structure rather than pricing bravado.

Against that: several material metrics were withheld (GCC revenue share, data-AI-cloud exact percentage, annuity share, Novigo standalone contribution, severance quantum, capex, net debt), and the answers on organic growth were more re-framing than disclosure — *"we have consistently shown organic growth quarter-over-quarter over last many quarters"* was offered with no organic number attached. One misstatement to note: *"we have managed to provide almost 18% quarter-over-quarter growth despite or without any real headcount change"* — QoQ growth was **1.2% in USD / 4.7% in INR**; the ~18% figure is the **YoY dollar** number (17.7%), which he states correctly minutes later (*"18% increase year on year in revenue without any uptake in headcount"*). Treat it as a slip, not a claim.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Management guided the margin *down* while printing a record — that is the single most informative line on the call.** 20.1% delivered, 18–19% reaffirmed as sustainable. The gap is roughly the size of the FX and utilisation tailwinds, and they said so. Modelling 20% forward is modelling against the company's own view.
- **R Systems' structural weakness is currently its best defence.** The absence of multi-year annuity contracts — normally the criticism levelled at it — is precisely why it escapes the AI-renewal deflation now compressing large-cap IT: *"we are not doing multi-year contracts or year-on-year renewals where it is obvious that customers would in fact expect AI-led productivity gains."* If the agentic business-ops push succeeds in building annuity, it will **import** that deflation risk. The two goals are in tension and nobody on the call named it.
- **The AI story is showing up in gross margin, not revenue.** Revenue per employee is up (headcount flat, revenue up), gross margin +320bps, utilisation held. But USD revenue grew only 1.2% QoQ and TTM ACV is flat. So far AI has made the existing book more profitable rather than made the book bigger — and management effectively concedes the revenue effect is still ahead: *"that mix will have to change quite significantly for it to show up as a line item on our overall results."*
- **The Q4→Q1 PAT "decline" is a base artefact and will reverse out of the optics next quarter.** Q4 FY26 carried an INR18 cr one-time hedging-policy benefit; adjusted PAT −17.1% QoQ measures against that. Operationally EBITDA rose 4.4% QoQ.
- **Hedge accounting has moved FX volatility from the P&L to OCI — but only until contracts mature.** The INR18.04 cr fair-value loss sat in OCI; this quarter maturities began reclassifying accumulated losses *back* into P&L plus a INR9 cr realised loss. The P&L is now smoother in the middle and lumpier at the edges, and other income is the line where it lands.
- **Novigo was bought for a capability, and the capability is what is compounding.** Its RPA/low-code/no-code enterprise-process DNA is the input to agentic business ops — *"we have jointly been able to bring out a bunch of agentic business AI operations offerings, which is what we are seeing as the green shoots."* Judging Novigo on its revenue contribution misses the point management is making.
- **The GCC offering is both a market and a competitor.** R Systems monetises captives becoming innovation hubs (HFS Horizon 2 recognition, one win this quarter is a GCC build) — while the same captive-GCC wave is what displaces traditional offshore vendors. Being paid to build the thing that disintermediates your industry is an unusually good position, and it is why the GCC line matters more than its (undisclosed) revenue share suggests.
- **APAC's decline is the honest read on project-business risk.** A single cohort of large projects ending moved the geography mix by ~2 points in one quarter. That is the volatility embedded in a discretionary book, visible in the actual numbers rather than in the risk paragraph.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Interest expense stepped up sharply to INR 94.8M in Q2 2026 (INR 190.7M in H1 2026) from INR 21.4M in Q2 2025 (INR 36.3M in H1 2025); the deck does not explain the increase.
- Q2 2025 non-recurring income of INR 409.3M is described as "profit on sale of land, building and certain other assets located at Company's NOIDA office as offset by finding fees paid for Chief Revenue Officer"; Q2 2026 and Q1 2026 non-recurring items are severance payments.
- Depreciation and amortization rose to INR 220.4M in Q2 2026 and INR 435.4M in H1 2026 from INR 158.4M and INR 304.5M respectively a year earlier.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Geography (revenue mix):** **Americas 71.5%** (up from 69.3%), **APAC 15.3%** (down — *"due to some of the larger projects that we were running in the last quarter that came to an end"*), **Europe 9.7%** (flat), **Middle East & Africa 3.6%** (flat).
- **Client concentration:** top client **6.0%** (from 5.8%), top 10 **24.4%** (from 24.0%). Management reads the *increase* as positive mining, not risk: *"while we do not have a significant client concentration risk, the continued efforts on mining and growing existing accounts continue to create recurring revenues."* Wallet share in the **top 50** also rose, driven by AI-led modernisation and, in BFSI, AI business-ops.
- **Novigo.** Integration is **done**: *"we did that integration in the middle of Q4 and completed that for the full quarter in Q1."* Its strategic contribution is capability, not just revenue — it was bought for *"their deeper understanding of enterprise landscapes and enterprise business flows"* across insurance, banking and travel/transportation, and prior **RPA / low-code / no-code** business-operations experience, which is what has been recombined into the agentic business-ops offering. Management insists ACV growth is not acquisition-flattered: *"our ACV wins or the growth itself is not influenced by the acquisition… both organizations are continuing to play in the same manner."* It carries a live problem — *"Novigo, of course, has an ongoing geopolitical challenge that they are dealing with, which is due to the geopolitical situation in the Middle East."*
- **Data, AI and cloud — now the majority of the business:** *"as an organization, we have now significantly data AI and cloud services-driven organization, revenue numbers have crossed 50% and continues to go up."* Characterised as *"largely transformation or innovation-led initiatives"*, project-lifecycle driven but **not seasonal**.
- **Annuity revenue: still small.** *"we have started seeing some bit of annuity, but it is, primarily being an engineering service provider… that portion of revenue is still not very high."*
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **AI productivity delivered as a quantified, priced-in outcome.** *"we are able to deliver almost **2x productivity and 55% gains in turnaround time** to our customers… from using our Optima AI platform."* Crucially management claims it is monetised rather than surrendered: *"we are able to continue to charge premium for delivering such AI-led productivity through our solutions."*
- **Structural immunity to AI price deflation — via the absence of annuity.** *"we do not have that deflationary effect because we are not doing multi-year contracts or year-on-year renewals where it is obvious that customers would in fact expect AI-led productivity gains… For us, the AI-based productivity is an inbuilt part of our AI-first delivery methodology. So, what we bid for and what we win in the market is AI-led and already contains the elements of productivity gains."*
- **Third-party validation of the GCC offering** — **HFS Horizon 2 GCC Accelerator** in the *Horizon GCC Services 2026* report; *"Our portfolio proprietary accelerators have been recognized as a key differentiator."*
- **Operating evidence of the claim.** Revenue up materially *"despite or without any real headcount change"*, gross margin 36% → 39.2%, utilisation held in-band — i.e. the productivity claim shows in the P&L, not only in the pitch.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Recognised as a "Horizon 2 GCC Accelerator in HFS' Horizons: GCC Services, 2026 Report", which the deck calls "Validation of our AI-first GCC model and platform-led delivery".
- The deck claims a proprietary moat: "Our portfolio of proprietary accelerators have been recognized as key differentiators enabling GCCs in this transformation".
- Demand thesis framed around three 2026 trends: organisations weighing "the cost of running AI" and turning to "expert product engineering providers like RSI to architect AI efficient end to end systems"; "Legacy Modernization continues to be a very large total addressable market (TAM) across legacy code bases, legacy data estates and reporting landscapes"; and enterprises seeing "Engineering Velocity as key differentiator for achieving return on investment (ROI) from AI Initiatives".
- Delivery is heavily Americas-weighted: Revenue by Geography Americas 71.5% in Q2 2026 vs 69.3% in Q1 2026, APAC 15.3% vs 17.5%, Europe 9.7% vs 9.6%, MEA 3.6% vs 3.6%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] The deck references "the new acquisition of Novigo" only in a DSO footnote — DSO is computed excluding Novigo. No deal size, date, capability or financial contribution is disclosed anywhere in the deck.
- [Accounting] "Effective 1 January 2026, the Company designated certain foreign currency forward contracts as cash flow hedges under Ind AS 109. The effective portion of changes in fair value has been recognised in the Hedge Reserve under equity which will be reclassified to profit and loss account when the corresponding hedged transactions occur."
- [Accounting] On the same adoption the deck states "other income for Q1 2026 was higher by Rs.180.47 million, as changes in the fair value of designated hedging instruments were recognized in Other Comprehensive Income (OCI)" — quoted as written; the deck does not reconcile the "higher by" wording with recognition in OCI.
- [Reporting calendar] R Systems reports on a calendar year (Q2 CY 2026, CY 2025 comparatives), not an Indian fiscal year.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
Gross margin moved **36.0% → 39.2%** on three named drivers: *"higher billable dates, rupee depreciation and improved utilization"* (80.5% → 81%). Adjusted EBITDA of 20.1% is attributed to *"operating leverages, improved revenue mix and favorable exchange rates."* Against that, **SG&A rose INR23.8 cr QoQ to INR115.3 cr**, which is deliberate and ongoing: a **Chief Revenue Officer** was hired, AI and domain experts were added into the sales process (*"it is no longer enough to have just pure sales people in the market"*), and marketing spend went into the new brand identity and the EXIQO launch — *"deliberate increase in sales and marketing and we continue to stay focused."*

The honest part of the margin story is that management refuses to own all of it. Asked to explain the improvement, Nitesh Bansal named revenue-mix and revenue-per-employee first, then immediately conceded: *"that number may not be by itself sufficient to account for the entire margin increase because quite a large portion of it also comes from the Forex or exchange rate or rupee depreciation, which we cannot take for granted. It is beyond our control. So, we will take benefit of it while it happens."* That, plus the reaffirmed **18–19%** sustainable band against **20.1%** delivered, is management telling you the run-rate is lower. Below EBITDA, **ETR at ~31% vs a normalized 28–29%** is a permanent drag while acquisition intangibles amortise (**INR10.6 cr of the INR22 cr D&A**), and **interest of INR9.5 cr a quarter** is a standing acquisition-funding cost.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this) — company's "Q2 & H1 2026":** *(our previous note was **Q3 FY25**, so this entry spans six quarters; comparatives are management's own.)* Record print — revenue **INR601.7 cr (+30.2% INR / +17.7% USD YoY; +4.7% / +1.2% QoQ)**, adjusted EBITDA **INR120.7 cr at 20.1% (+281 bps YoY, flat QoQ)**, gross margin **36% → 39.2%**, adjusted PAT **INR62.9 cr (+35.4% YoY, −17.1% QoQ off an INR18 cr hedging-benefit base)**, reported PAT **INR55.6 cr**. H1 CY26 revenue **INR1,176.5 cr (+30.1%)**, adjusted PAT **INR138.7 cr (+54.4%)**. **Novigo is now fully integrated** (mid-Q4 CY25, full quarter from Q1 CY26) — status changed from "acquisition pending" in our Q3 FY25 card — and is the capability source for the new **agentic business operations** line. **Margin guide reaffirmed at 18–19% adjusted EBITDA, below the 20.1% delivered**, with management attributing "quite a large portion" of the gain to rupee depreciation. **Hedge accounting adopted last quarter** (INR18.04 cr fair-value loss to OCI; INR9 cr realised loss on forward settlement this quarter; cover $43.32 mn @ INR93.27 vs spot INR94.66). **TTM ACV flat at $82.9 mn vs $82.3 mn.** Headcount roughly flat YoY while revenue grew; utilisation 80.5% → 81%; DSO 55–56 days billed. New this quarter: **EXIQO AI Studio** launched with a new brand identity (claimed **2x productivity, 55% turnaround-time gains** via Optima AI), **HFS Horizon 2 GCC Accelerator** recognition, **Chief Revenue Officer** hired, **data-AI-cloud crossed 50% of revenue**, five named AI-first wins (telecom analytics, US small-business-lender GCC, insurance AI quality engineering, exchanges CRM on Dynamics 365, ad-tech core modernisation). Americas up to **71.5%**, APAC down to **15.3%** on projects ending. Wage hike (first of two biannual cycles) **already absorbed** in this quarter. **No revenue guidance; no capex, net-debt or cash figure disclosed; no hard-dated near-term catalyst.**
- _Q2 FY27 → check: did adjusted EBITDA fall back into the guided **18–19%** band as management signalled, and how much of any decline is FX vs reinvestment; did **TTM ACV break out of the ~$82–83 mn plateau** (two flat quarters now); did the H1-bookings→H2-revenue lag actually deliver sequential USD acceleration above +1.2%; did **constant-currency growth reach the 3–4% aspiration** or stay near 2%; the **second biannual wage-hike cycle** — when, and what margin cost; further **forward-contract settlement losses** as the $43.32 mn book at INR93.27 matures against spot; whether **data-AI-cloud share** is disclosed above 50% and whether **annuity revenue becomes reportable** off agentic business ops; any quantification of **GCC revenue share**; Novigo Middle East geopolitical situation; whether another **acquisition** moves from "on the lookout" to announced; ETR back toward the normalized 28–29%._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Revenue growth: NO guidance, stated twice and unambiguously.** *"as you know, we do not provide guidance"* and *"anyway, we do not provide forward-looking guidance."* The only forward framing offered is a mechanical lag: *"Our bookings of last half become revenues for this half. Our whole effort on sales and marketing is all setting up for creating ACV wins in this half, which will become revenues in the next half."* Asked directly whether that means a better H2, management agreed only in principle — *"that is the revenue realization that is how we look at it"* — with **no number and no date**.
- **Margin — the one hard guide, and it is DOWN from delivered:** *"like I have guided in the past also, we continue to stay focused to stay in that **18 to 19 percentage adjusted EBITDA on a sustainable basis**, beyond which we will obviously continue to invest in our AI initiatives, sales and marketing efforts."* Delivered this quarter: **20.1%**. Management is explicitly signalling that ~120bps of the current margin is not banked.
- **Constant-currency growth — aspiration, not guidance, and explicitly hedged.** Asked when CC growth returns to the 3–4% range: *"given that the numbers are not very large, a small deviation obviously changes it to 2% or so… the biggest factor over there continues to be the decision cycles… it is only a matter of time."* **No date.**
- **Order inflow / ACV target:** declined. *"can you provide some quantifiable guidance on deal wins for the upcoming quarters?"* → *"Well, like I said, very difficult to say."* Only qualitative: *"the quality of pipeline is better, meaning average deal sizes is better."*
- **Wage hike — already absorbed, not a forward risk this quarter:** *"We have implemented a wage hike in this quarter. We carry out biannual wage hike cycles. Our first cycle has already taken place and the impact of that has already come in this quarterly results."* The **second biannual cycle was not dated**.
- **Capex / commissioning dates:** none disclosed on this call.
- **Undisclosed metrics management declined to quantify:** GCC revenue share (*"I do not think we have disclosed the percentage of revenue separately"*), data-AI-cloud exact share (only *"revenue numbers have crossed 50% and continues to go up"*), annuity revenue share (*"that portion of revenue is still not very high"*).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
Not an order-book business; the disclosed forward metric is **trailing-12-month ACV bookings**, which came in at **$82.9 mn vs $82.3 mn in Q1 — effectively flat**, and this was the single most-pressed point of the call. Management's defence is a base effect: *"if you look back at four quarters ago, last year we had few large deal wins in Q2. This year again, we have had a few large deal wins in Q2, which has effectively filled up for what would have been a significant ACV uptick Q2 last year."* Asked whether flat ACV signalled slowing decisions or weak discretionary spend, the answer was *"In fact, Sandeep, neither of the two"* — the TTM series *"continues to show that we are at least winning as much as we were winning in the past or slightly more."*

**Five named wins this quarter, all framed as AI-first:**
1. **Leading global telecom player** — advanced analytics, data science and intelligent solutions for actionable business insights.
2. **Small-business lender (large financial institution)** — building *"a center of excellence, sort of a GCC in India"* covering product engineering, software engineering and digital operations to *"fuel the AI-powered lending innovation."*
3. **Large global insurance & financial services provider** — AI-powered quality engineering and testing enhancement for their high-net-worth client platform.
4. **Global financial services organisation in market access & exchanges** — retail transformation, CRM/customer experience on **Microsoft Dynamics 365** with omni-channel integration, acquisition-to-onboarding lifecycle modernisation.
5. **Leading ad-tech company** — full AI-led modernisation of a complex ad-distribution core platform *"without any disruption to their existing clients and everyday operations of ad spend."*

*"As you would have noted, all of these wins indicate a very AI first stance."* Both **deal size and duration** are said to be increasing: *"both our size of the wins, as well as duration has continued to increase."*
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Agentic business operations** — the clearest new growth vector, and the explicit rationale for Novigo. *"The agentic business operations side of service offerings has been seeing a lot of traction. This comes on the back of our deep domain understanding and investment in building agentic AI ecosystems."* It is also the stated path to a **reportable annuity line**: *"as we build our book of business over there, we might be able to have a reportable annuity revenue at some point of time."*
- **GCC enablement** — recognised as a **Horizon 2 GCC Accelerator by HFS in their Horizon GCC Services 2026 report**, a year and a half after launching the offering. The demand driver: *"global capability centers existing in India continue to be challenged by their parent organizations to become innovation hubs and engines to lead AI-based and platform-based delivery."* One of this quarter's five wins is itself a GCC build for a US small-business lender.
- **AI-led modernisation** — *"legacy modernization… continues to be a large TAM across legacy code bases, data estates, and reporting landscapes"*, and *"a recurring theme across our wins in the market."*
- **AI-cost architecture** — a distinct emerging service: *"organizations are looking at cost of running AI as a very important factor and turning towards experts like R Systems to look at how do we architect AI-efficient ecosystems so that while they gain AI efficiencies… they should not have huge financial costs to incur for using that AI."*
- **EXIQO AI Studio** (exiqo.ai) — launched alongside a new brand identity; *"has been getting a lot of traction. We have been invited to several conferences."*
- **Channel play** — *"we are working more with private equities, we are working more with hyper scalers and channel partners"*, cited as a reason the revenue mix has shifted toward strategic client spend.
- **Ecosystem partnerships** — *"we continue to strengthen our ecosystem partnership with startups and technology companies"* for capabilities not built in-house.
